title: These Are Not Defiled With Women Part 2

sense.text:
“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning.” Everything that was written aforetime is in the Bible, and all of it is for our learning. That also says you are supposed to rule your house with the scriptures, not with your hands. In Israel there are husbands that beat on their wives, and there are wives that put hands on their husbands too. Some brothers keep it quiet because it is embarrassing. Sisters, if you are doing that you got the devil on you and you need to repent. It doesn’t matter if it is a man or a woman: when you get caught, you will be put out.

Look through the scriptures: not one of the examples our forefathers left behind shows them beating their wives. Some of our forefathers argued with their wives, but not one time did any of them put hands on them. There is going to be argument; you got two different spirits in the same house, so there will be disagreement. But nothing is so bad that a leader should put hands on his wife. If it gets so heated that you feel you have to, you might have married the wrong person.

“That we through patience”: some of you have no patience with your wives, some of you have no patience with your husbands, and some of you have no patience with your children. “And comfort of the scriptures”: you find your comfort and your peace in the scriptures, and only the scriptures can bring peace into the house. The scripture is supposed to bring peace, comfort and joy into the household. If the only time there is peace is when you bring the scriptures, or there is a fight every time it is brought, that means somebody in the house does not believe. A brother said every time he burned incense in his house there was an argument; that means one of you in the house is the devil who cannot stand the smell, and it was his wife who did not believe.

The biggest problem in the black community today is relationships, and our goal is to stop the foolishness going on in black marriages. The church is not going to stop it; the Christian church does not teach about marriage at all, and wants the black woman single because most of its finances come from the single black woman. But when you repent and call yourself a leader in Israel, leadership starts at the house. Leadership does not start in the church.

“Now therefore set thine house in order, and reprove thy people.” Set your house in order first. You cannot go in the street, reprove thy people and try to win back Israel while your house is in chaos; that makes you a hypocrite. If you cannot run your wife and your children, how are you going to run the nation of Israel? The church starts in your house, with your wife and children. Have control over that first, and only then can you reprove thy people, tell a brother he shall not commit adultery, and teach. Don’t be scared to take control because she will hold back from you; the scripture says a wife is not supposed to hold from her husband, and the Most High will move that out of the way. Have the faith to believe what the scripture says instead of going back and forth.

“Comfort such of them as be in trouble.” Your comfort comes from the scriptures, so how are you going to comfort those in trouble when you don’t believe the scripture yourself? Our people are in deep trouble, and you are the ones who can comfort them. Not the false leaders buying private jets, not Trump. Republican or Democrat, nothing is going to change for our people unless we comfort them with the scriptures, and the Christian church is not going to change it. Brothers, you are the leaders; it is your job.

It is only going to get worse. In 1950, 64% of black men and 62% of black women were married; in 2021 only 31.2% of black people in the US were married. Back then they had little, ten children in a two bedroom house on one income, plastic on the furniture, and still they made it work, with the wife cooking for the husband after his twelve and fourteen hour shift. The enemy is behind the fall of the black family. He set the trap and we fell right into it, like the movie Claudine, where the welfare policy put the man out of the house. You cannot build a nation without family. The kingdom of God is for families, men, women and children: we came here in slavery with the woman and we are leaving with the woman.

Incarceration and systemic barriers keep black men from marriage, and the chance of going back to jail once you have been is high, because Esau set it up like that. Those systemic barriers are unfair policies against our people and our families. The war in Genesis is between Jacob and Esau, so what makes you think Esau is going to pass any policy in favour of Jacob? The chain is not broken by voting Democrat, Republican or independent. It can only be broken with the Bible, and you are the ones who can break it. The enemy will not like it and will come after us; if you die in this, you die for the love of your people, and that is a great honour.

“The burden of the word of the Lord to Israel by Malachi.” This is to us, Israel. We are Israelites.

The systemic barriers come from racism, and every Esau is racist. Every white person is racist; some of them, the educated ones, just know how to hide it well. Donald Trump is one politician who reveals how racist white people are, and that is why the Republican party cannot stand that they cannot control what he says. Esau is like somebody who throws a rock and hides his hand. If you want to make them mad, call them racist. But it is not made up; it is in the scripture.

“I have loved you, saith the Lord.” God says he loves us; he loved Jacob. “Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us?” We ask God how he loves us. “Was not Esau Jacob’s brother?” There is the question: yes, in the book of Genesis Jacob and Esau were brothers. “Saith the Lord: yet I loved Jacob.” They were brothers, but God loved Jacob, only Jacob.
“And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.” God said he hates Esau. He loves the one and hates the other.

“Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places; thus saith the Lord of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness.” And then “the people” against whom he has indignation: not some of them, not ten percent of them, the whole race of Esau. God says he hates them. God is the one who said it.

“For by means of a whorish woman a man is brought to a piece of bread.” A piece of bread is nothing. Can a piece of bread get you the kingdom of heaven? Some of you will lose the kingdom for a whorish woman.

“And the adulteress will hunt for the precious life.” Brothers, some of you don’t know you are that precious life. You are the prophets, the apostles; you are the Abraham, the Isaac, the Jacob, the Moses, Jeremiah and Nehemiah. Some sisters are here to destroy you, because having a Bible in their hand does not mean they are not here to destroy you. And it goes both ways: sisters, you are the daughters of Sarah, you are the Esther and the Susanna, and some brothers are here to destroy you and bring you to a piece of bread too. Some come here for a wife, not for the right reason, and we have seen it.

precepts.why:
Remember the name of the class: “These are they which were not defiled with women.” The men brought down to a piece of bread are the ones defiled with women.

You are defiled with women when you cannot control the household. You put a decision in place, your wife overrides it, you say nothing, and she keeps doing it. It is like a baby elephant in the house: you act like it is not there and it keeps growing, until the elephant is so big the house cannot contain it and it cannot even fit through the door, and now the whole wall has to come down to get it out. That is some of your marriages. When she did it the first time and you never corrected her, she learned it was okay.

A brother’s wife left him and said she did not want to be married to him any more; before the divorce was even over she laid down with her ex, and the brother went back and slept with her again. That brother is defiled, and if you don’t get that, that is why God cannot use you. And you want to come talking about shalom, I am officer of fifty: get the hell out of here. Some of your loyalty is to your penis. Your first loyalty is supposed to be to the Most High and your second to the brotherhood; if you have no loyalty to the Most High, how can you be trusted? When an evil thought pops into your mind you don’t have to do it. Tell yourself, shut the hell up. You are supposed to talk to your penis, not your penis talking to you; that is how you control it. Some of you let it control you, and it gets you in trouble one time, two times. How many times are you going to listen to that body part?

“They say, If a man put away his wife, and she go from him, and become another man’s.” Become another man’s means she slept with another man. Brothers, you don’t have to see it go in. If your wife is on social media talking to other men, texting other men back and forth, sending a naked picture to another man, her heart is knit to somebody else. Kissing another man, hugging another man, feeling another man: it ain’t got to go in. Stop being a damn fool. No man should be doing to your wife what is only meant for you to do to her, not one thing. And if you do see it, that is trauma that scars you the rest of your life. If you are waiting to see it before you believe, the Bible cannot help you.

“Shall he return unto her again? shall not that land be greatly polluted?” Polluted means made unsuitable or unsafe, poisoned, contaminated, adulterated, tainted, impure, made dirty. That ex-wife has been polluted. That coochie is unsafe: STDs, HIV, herpes, syphilis, and a negro spirit in there too. God said the coochie has been poisoned, and when you take poison you die; brother, you have been poisoned. It is contaminated, adulterated, tainted by another man. When food is recalled because it is contaminated, nobody goes back to buy it, because it can pollute you, but some will go back to the vagina that God said is polluted.

You cannot go back to the defiled. Don’t be the simp who keeps going back to the defiled bread, crying that it hurts a lot: she is not your woman any more. Bishop Nathanyel always says you don’t really know a brother until he gets married, and it has proven true over and over. These are things happening in the body, among repented Israelite brothers who wore the purple and gold, going back to the defiled bread. Don’t laugh like it can’t be you.

Read the rest of verse 26 and go down to verse 32: “But whoso committeth adultery with a woman lacketh understanding.” A brother or a sister who commits adultery lacks understanding of the law, of what the Bible says. Don’t be that brother.

“He that doeth it destroyeth his own soul.” That means you are going to die and you are not going to get the kingdom. Is it really worth it for five minutes? Some of you only got two pumps; you are going to lose the kingdom for that? Some of you put in mighty work, God sees your work, and you would throw all of that away for five minutes. That is the piece of bread the whorish woman brings a man to.

sense.text: “Marriage is honourable in all.” To be married and bear children is the honourable thing. Brothers, do not turn our sisters into whores. Some of you have that spirit on you and think you are going to come in here and do that; it is not going to happen. Some sisters come here to get their lives right and in order, and we will help in every way possible to make sure you don’t destroy them. Bishop always said this is a hospital: you come here to get healed.

precepts.why:
Christ said it himself. “As Jesus sat at meat in the house, behold, many publicans and sinners came and sat down with him and his disciples.” The Pharisees asked, “Why eateth your Master with publicans and sinners?”

“They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick.” If you say you are whole, you are saying you are not a sinner, that you have no sin in you, and then Christ did not come for you. We are a house full of sick people, a hospital. We all came here because we are sick and need healing, and the only healing is through the scriptures: the law is what is going to heal us, if you apply it. Don’t be a hearer only, be a doer.

The sisters came to be healed and the brothers came to be healed, so why would you want to destroy them? If you want to destroy them, you are saying you are not sick, and a man who is not sick does not go to the doctor. A brother who chases his woman down in the parking lot after catching her in the act has a sick spirit too. And many want to rush a brother or sister who is still on the operating table, with a broken spirit that has not had time to heal. When leadership says leave that one alone, it is not hating or blocking your blessing.

sense.text: “Be in peace with many: nevertheless have but one counsellor of a thousand.” The problem with a lot of you is that you don’t have a counsellor. Don’t do it first and then ask for counsel; before you even say hi to a sister, ask for counsel first. And counsel up: you cannot take counsel from somebody who came in two months ago like you. Ask a captain what he knows of that sister. If she has only been here a year, a good counsellor says give her another year: the first year is the best behaviour, and in the second you start to see how that spirit works, around other sisters and in the office. You got all the time in the world; if she is for you she isn’t going nowhere. What God put together let no man put asunder, but some of you God did not put together: you went through the back door, and when you did your back door business you took no counsel, so don’t come looking for leadership now.

“If thou wouldest get a friend, prove him first.” A brother from the world invited into your house cannot go in your fridge and start drinking your things, and cannot walk into your bedroom and sit on your bed; there are places he cannot go. It is the same when you are proving for marriage. The person you decide to marry is one of the biggest decisions in this truth. Mighty brothers who know the scriptures left and right, great teachers, make horrible decisions with women, and the person you marry can drain the spirit out of you. That person is who you will spend the rest of your life with.

Nearly everybody you start talking to tells you what you want to hear; give them six months or a year and ask the same question again, and you will see a difference. Show me who your friends are and I’ll show you who you are: a sister who only keeps company with single sisters, none of them married, gets nothing that builds her mind for marriage, while the married sister would tell her the reality. Some want to be married but not in a marriage, a husband but not a lord. There are no white horses and no fairy tale in marriage. Take your time. Brothers, say it: I’m the prize.

“And be not hasty to credit him.” When a brother or sister walks in from the street they are broken, and our job is to rebuild them, but nobody builds a house in one day; it is built brick by brick. Some come from the homosexual lifestyle, some from the lesbian lifestyle, and those spirits take years to rebuild. A married sister divorced and went back to that life, and brothers have gone back too, because nobody gave them time to heal. They come from a filthy, disgusting lifestyle, so do not be hasty to credit them.

precepts.why:
For the one who would not take counsel and comes running to leadership afterward: “Now therefore keep thy sorrow to thyself, and bear with a good courage that which hath befallen thee.” Keep your sorrow to yourself; these things have nothing to do with leadership.

When you did it without counsel and then show up in front of the Deacon with your troubles, this is the scripture that will be read to you. You don’t have to be told shalom: once that scripture is read to you, say thank you and goodbye. It means goodbye brother, goodbye sis. Bear a good courage: you’ll be alright.

“Go not after thy lusts, but refrain thyself from thine appetites.” In the whole process of proving a friend, you have to know what lust is within you. Often you rush the process and get caught up in all kinds of jams because you went after your lust, with no plan of growing old with that sister, or that brother.

“Wine and women will make men of understanding to fall away.” Go not after your lust, because wine and women make a man of understanding lose all sense of reality and common sense; he may know the scripture, but applying it goes out the window. “And he that cleaveth to harlots will become impudent”: if your appetite is harlots you become rude and hard-minded.

So the scripture says go not after thy lust, refrain from your appetites, and then it says wine and women will make men of understanding fall away.

Verse four is the point: “He that is hasty to give credit is lightminded; and he that sinneth shall offend against his own soul.” Why would you be hasty to give credit? Because you went after your lust and did not refrain from your appetite; a man of understanding is ready to fall because of that lust, so gung-ho to give credit to somebody he doesn’t even know, fully engulfed in going after his lust. Lightminded is simple. If you are proving a friend, you are proving them for the long haul.

Some of you have been fighting pornography for years; how come you still have that spirit? Because spirits do not just leave. Christ said, “Howbeit this kind goeth not out but by prayer and fasting.” Why would Christ put that there if the spirit just left?

Some of those spirits take time, brothers and sisters. That is why it says be not hasty to credit them: there is a chance those spirits can come back.

A friend is a person whom one knows, and it takes time to know somebody; meeting someone does not make you friends. Sisters who tell all their business to a sister who has been here two months, calling her my friend: sister, you’re an idiot. Look what your friendship should be based on: “But be continually with a godly man, whom thou knowest to keep the commandments of the Lord.”

Who you know is the one keeping the commandments of the Lord; that is a friend. Your friendship is not supposed to be based on gossip, or on mutual hatred of another brother or sister you are talking about. It is supposed to be based on the commandments of the Lord.

A friend is also one with whom one has a bond of mutual affection, which takes knowing. A sister says a brother who loves the Lord, puts in work and has his own house is not her type, when she never even said hi to him or gave him a chance (you idiot); yet the two baby daddies she picked herself were her type, and her father did not pick them for her.

sense.text: “A drunken woman and a gadder abroad causeth great anger, and she will not cover her own shame.” Brothers and sisters blame it on the alcohol. Sisters, there is nothing uglier, nastier or more disgusting than a drunken woman. This is not talking about a glass of wine or a drink; it is talking about a drunken woman. When she is drunk she gets nasty, mean-spirited and belligerent, wants to fight and starts cursing people out loud. It has happened here: a sister snuck a big bottle of liquor in between her legs to Passover.

Brothers, every one of you knows your limit: two and you are done, three and you are done. Get caught drunk on the road and you bring shame to the gospel, stumbling out of the car in your purple garments or feast day garments, maybe after hurting somebody. Those are the little things that will save your life.

“Wine is as good as life to a man, if it be drunk moderately.” If you drink enough to get drunk, that is not moderate. Some argue with and curse their wives when drunk, some get violent; you destroy your marriage and your family because you cannot control your liquor, and most of all you lose the kingdom. For some it is weed, a sister getting high before she walked in to the Sabbath.

“What life is then to a man that is without wine?” Everybody wants to sip once in a while, but you must know how to control yourself. “For it was made to make men glad.” That is why they call it spirit: there is a spirit in it, and some people cannot handle even a glass. It was made to make men glad, not violent, not argumentative, not belligerent, not verbally abusive. If you find yourself in any of those spirits after drinking, you need to stop. A brother choking his wife and blaming the drinking cannot control himself, has no discipline, and is not a leader.

“Wine measurably drunk and in season bringeth gladness of the heart, and cheerfulness of the mind.” There is nothing wrong with having a drink, but know your measure, know your limits. Don’t pick up the bottle before Esau’s workplace where they know you are an Israelite; you bring shame to the gospel. How do you expect your family to repent when you show up drunk? Your sons and daughters take it in, and if you are abusing your wife when drunk you are abusing the kids too, if not physically then verbally.
“But wine drunken with excess maketh bitterness of the mind, with brawling and quarrelling.” Excess is when you don’t know how to control it. Brawling is fighting.
“Drunkenness increaseth the rage of a fool till he offend.” The Bible calls you a fool. We don’t want to hear that you were drunk, officer of ten or of fifty. There is no excuse.

precepts.why:
“Declare unto us your mind concerning the writings. Then began the first, who had spoken of the strength of wine”. He is declaring the strength of wine. “It turneth also every thought into jollity and mirth, so that a man remembereth neither sorrow nor debt.” Jollity is joy: wine turns your thoughts into joyful thoughts, a time of gladness. It is supposed to make you merry, so you forget sorrow and the debt you are in.

But past a certain limit you become violent and your whole spirit changes, and that is the time to stop. “And when they are in their cups, they forget their love both to friends and brethren, and a little after draw out swords.” All of a sudden the brother you were drinking with is about to fight you; you forget that is your brother because of liquor. Many of us know people in our neighbourhoods and families who got drunk and nearly put each other to death, and here it is in the Holy Bible.

If you know you are an angry drunk, stop drinking. If you know you are a sobbing, weeping ass brother, stop drinking. If the liquor makes you start pouring out your heart and making everybody sorrowful, keep your sorrow to yourself and stop drinking.

A history of one of our forefathers and drunkenness. Simon was set up: “So when Simon and his sons had drunk largely, Ptolemee and his men rose up, and took their weapons, and came upon Simon into the banqueting place, and slew him, and his two sons.” Notice it says he had drunk largely.

Yes, he was set up to be killed, but he might have had a chance if he was not drunk. When you are drunk you are not in control, and that is how the enemy comes; it is the same as getting behind the wheel drunk. It was the same over the rape in the days of Levi: the men were circumcised and had no control, and they came and killed them all; and the revolution in Haiti started when they let the French get drunk and then moved in. Read the history of Maccabees: that is about our forefathers.

At the feast days, brothers serving should keep their eyes open for those who keep coming back for more. Be your brother’s keeper: pull the brother to the side and tell him he doesn’t need any more, and don’t let each other leave your houses intoxicated.

sense.text: “Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth.” Mortify your members means subdue them, control your members. “Fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection”: inordinate affection is having sex with a goat, sleeping in the same bed with the chicken, pedophilia. Why would the Most High put that in there? Because he knows those are the things his people have in them. If you are in the midst of that, repent and change. “Evil concupiscence, and covetousness, which is idolatry.” Control, subdue those spirits and the mind: just because you think it does not mean you have to do it.

precepts.why: “For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men.” If you get caught up in this stuff, fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, that is ungodliness and unrighteousness, and the wrath of God is revealed against it.

sense.text:
“Now the works of the flesh are manifest.” The works of the flesh, not the works of the spirit. We are all in the flesh, so stay in the spirit, as Bishop says; if you stay in the spirit you are not going to do what the flesh tells you to do. Adultery, fornication, uncleanness, lasciviousness, idolatry, witchcraft, hatred, variance, emulations, wrath, strife, seditions, heresies: all the work of the flesh.

“Envyings”: there are camps envying the Bishop. Envy builds hatred, and hatred creates blindness, until you are blind to the truth; you need to go to the Most High and ask for forgiveness. Some of them never met the Bishop or sat down with him, and when you ask why they hate him they don’t know. They hate you because of the purple and gold. Those are the works of the flesh; they do not come from the Most High. Christians say God told me; Satan told you, God didn’t tell you a damn thing. Negro please, the devil told you; the devil is right in your house. God did not tell you to hate your brother or call him out of his name. You can say the right name and have hatred in your heart.

“Murders”: hatred is murder. When you hate your brother that is murder; some of you hate your wife, some sisters hate their husbands, talking about him behind his back while he pays all the bills. “Drunkenness”: that is the work of the flesh. Christ never got drunk and abused the church, so why are you drunk and abusing your wife and children?

“Of the which I tell you before, as I have also told you in time past.” Paul told us before and he is telling us again. “That they which do such things shall not inherit the kingdom of God.” Those in the midst of these things will not get the kingdom. Fix it. Some kick the habit quickly, some take time, but work at it until you walk away from it. If you are still fighting the pornography spirit, that is a spirit: fast and pray that the Most High removes that spirit from you.

“But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace.” This is the work of the spirit. Love: love that brother as you love yourself. Joy: when you read the scripture it is supposed to bring joy to your relationship, your household, your wife and your children, not fighting and going back and forth. Peace: after that fourteen hour shift, when you walk through the door of those four walls you pay for, it is supposed to be peace, because at that job there was no peace.

“Longsuffering” is being patient. Be patient with your wife and with the kids; she is not going to get it the way you get it, and some of those children’s minds are caught up in social media. “Gentleness”: don’t confuse gentleness with being soft. Being gentle with your wife does not mean she thinks you are a punk.

precepts.why:
Gentleness backed up: “Finally, be ye all of one mind.” You and your wife are to be of the same mind: her mind after your mind, and your mind after Christ’s mind. “Having compassion one of another”: this is going into being gentle with your wife. “Love as brethren, be pitiful”: she is coming out of a mind state just like you are, so practise being gentle with her and show mercy when mercy is to be shown.

“Be courteous.” Some brothers don’t know how to be courteous; some are lions in the house, abusive in the house. These things will enhance your marriage: you get the most out of your wife if you practise what was just read, but some beat down her spirit so badly she doesn’t want to cook or clean or do anything for you. And some brothers don’t know how to receive peace, and when it is shown to them they think it is a setup. She is not trying to set you up.

sense.text:
“In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours.” The unity of brethren is a beautiful thing; love that brother as you love yourself.

“A man and a wife that agree together.” To agree together is to agree in the scriptures together. It does not mean she overrides your rule and you agree to it. A brother said don’t let the sick children out to play in the snow; she opened the door and sent them out, the children got sick, and then she could not find him to buy their medicine, saying she was saving him from his bad decisions. Some of these sisters are simple as hell. You handpicked him, you opened your legs to him: he is yours, bad decision or not.

If you are beating on her, you cannot be agreeing together. Sisters, if you are hitting your husband, you cannot be agreeing together. If you are going through that, your marriage was not put together by God. We expect disagreement and argument in every marriage, but when it goes physical, God did not put that together; you did, and now you live by your decision. Don’t go on social media blaming leadership: nobody from the body argued in your bed with you; that is on the two of you.

precepts.why:
“Give me any plague, but the plague of the heart: and any wickedness, but the wickedness of a woman.” Any wickedness but the wickedness of a woman: that is some evil stuff, like the woman caught in the video.

A sister like that comes here looking for a husband, and the answer is no: you need time. Single brothers, when that sister was here she did not look at any of you, you were not good enough, not her type. She went out in the world, got pregnant by a negro out there, and now she is back struggling with the baby and the bills, looking for a husband to pay them. Don’t be a simp, sitting there with a cape on. There are many sisters in this body who put in a lot of work; give them your time.

sense.text: “To depart from wickedness is a thing pleasing to the Lord.” To depart from evil, to depart from your sin, is a beautiful thing; that thing pleases the Lord. “And to forsake unrighteousness is a propitiation.” To forsake sin. Propitiation is like an atonement, a payment, appeasing God: forsaking your sin is an atonement that pleases God.
